knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

```{r cars}
library(tidyverse)
library(keras3)
library(patchwork)
set_random_seed(2026)
raw_data <- readRDS("handwriting.rds")

# Scale pixel tensors directly from integer space to normalized floating bounds
x_all <- raw_data$images / 255
metadata <- as_tibble(raw_data$metadata)
```

##Explicit Data Partitioning & Out-of-Session Strategy
```{r task-4-partitioning}
#| label: data-split

# Explicit session-out grouping enforces generalization across distinct recording iterations
train_idx <- which(metadata$session %in% c(1, 2, 3))
val_idx   <- which(metadata$session == 4)
test_idx  <- which(metadata$session == 5)

x_train <- x_all[train_idx, , , , drop = FALSE]
x_val   <- x_all[val_idx, , , , drop = FALSE]
x_test  <- x_all[test_idx, , , , drop = FALSE]

# 0-indexing conversion for sparse categorical cross-entropy optimization targets
y_train_person <- as.integer(metadata$person_id[train_idx] - 1L)
y_val_person   <- as.integer(metadata$person_id[val_idx] - 1L)
y_test_person  <- as.integer(metadata$person_id[test_idx] - 1L)

# Cache tensor splits for synchronization across sub-group members
saveRDS(list(x = x_train, y = y_train_person), "train_split.rds")
saveRDS(list(x = x_val, y = y_val_person), "val_split.rds")
saveRDS(list(x = x_test, y = y_test_person, metadata = metadata[test_idx, ]), "test_split.rds")
```

The dataset was split by recording session, using Sessions 1–3 for training, Session 4 for validation, and Session 5 for testing. This strategy allows the CNN to learn writer-specific features from earlier sessions, use the validation set for model selection, and evaluate final performance on a later, unseen session.

This represents within-writer, across-session generalization, because the same 20 writers appear across all sets, but the test images come from a session excluded from training. It does not evaluate generalization to unseen writers.

Potential leakage could arise from duplicate or highly similar images across sessions or preprocessing that uses information from the entire dataset. Performance could also be optimistically biased if test results were repeatedly used to tune the model. Therefore, Session 5 should remain reserved for final evaluation, and image independence should be checked.

# Multi-Class CNN Writer Identification Architecture


```{r cnn-training, echo=FALSE}
#| label: cnn-model

cnn_model <- keras_model_sequential(input_shape = c(28, 28, 1)) %>%
  layer_conv_2d(filters = 32, kernel_size = c(3, 3), activation = "relu") %>%
  layer_max_pooling_2d(pool_size = c(2, 2)) %>%
  layer_conv_2d(filters = 64, kernel_size = c(3, 3), activation = "relu") %>%
  layer_max_pooling_2d(pool_size = c(2, 2)) %>%
  layer_flatten() %>%
  layer_dense(units = 128, activation = "relu") %>%
  layer_dropout(rate = 0.3) %>%
  layer_dense(units = 20, activation = "softmax")

cnn_model %>% compile(
  optimizer = optimizer_adam(learning_rate = 0.001),
  loss = "sparse_categorical_crossentropy",
  metrics = c("accuracy")
)

history_cnn <- cnn_model %>% fit(
  x_train, y_train_person,
  epochs = 8,
  batch_size = 64,
  validation_data = list(x_val, y_val_person),
  verbose = 1
)
```

## Model Evaluation and Performance Metrics
We assess how well the network holds up against completely unseen writing samples from Session 5.

```{r evaluations}
#| label: evaluation-metrics

probs <- cnn_model %>% predict(x_test)
preds <- apply(probs, 1, function(x) which.max(x) - 1L)

eval_df <- tibble(
  True_Writer = y_test_person + 1L,
  Pred_Writer = preds + 1L,
  Digit       = metadata$digit[test_idx]
)

overall_accuracy <- mean(
  eval_df$True_Writer == eval_df$Pred_Writer
)

print(overall_accuracy)
#overall_accuracy <- mean(eval_df\(True_Writer == eval_df\)Pred_Writer)
```

##Performance Breakdown by Digit Context

Below is the evaluation tracking accuracy context per individual numeric item:
```{r digit-table}

#| label: digit-performance-summary
#| echo: false

digit_breakdown <- eval_df %>%
  group_by(Digit) %>%
  summarize(
    Accuracy = mean(True_Writer == Pred_Writer),
    Total_Samples = n(),
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

knitr::kable(digit_breakdown, digits = 4)

saveRDS(eval_df, "cnn_predictions_output.rds")
```

##comparison of validation and test accuracy
```{r}
# CNN validation predictions: session 4
val_probs <- predict(cnn_model, x_val, verbose = 0)
val_preds <- apply(val_probs, 1, which.max)

cnn_val_accuracy <- mean(
  (val_preds - 1L) == y_val_person
)

# CNN test accuracy: session 5
cnn_test_accuracy <- mean(
  eval_df$True_Writer == eval_df$Pred_Writer
)

cnn_session_comparison <- tibble(
  Dataset = c("Validation: Session 4", "Test: Session 5"),
  Accuracy = c(cnn_val_accuracy, cnn_test_accuracy)
)

print(cnn_session_comparison)
```
